sources.title: Value Added Tax Brochure — what VAT is; the standard rate of 15 % and the zero rate on exports (§ 2); how VAT is calculated on a VAT-inclusive price (§ 4); the exempted supplies (§ 6); compulsory registration from D2,000,000 of taxable supplies in a tax year and voluntary registration from D1,000,000 (§ 7); de-registration (§ 9); monthly filing and payment on the 15th of the following month and import VAT payable before release (§ 10); refunds (§ 12). It states that it is not an exhaustive replacement of the VAT laws.

Domestic Taxes FAQs, VAT section — standard rate 15 %, zero rate on exports of goods and services, thresholds of D2,000,000 (compulsory) and D1,000,000 (voluntary) of taxable supplies in a tax year, monthly return due 15 days after the month end, filing at the nearest Domestic Taxes Department office, payment at a DTD office or a partner bank, input VAT credit and refunds
GRA Online Services — the Authority's page for its electronic services; it links the tax calculators and the Domestic Taxes Department, and does not itself name a VAT return filing function

Use of IFRS Standards by jurisdiction — The Gambia: IFRS Standards required for commercial banks and permitted for all other companies; IFRS for SMEs not adopted but SMEs are permitted to use it; the Companies Act 1955 does not specify the accounting standards; the Gambia Institute of Chartered Accountants and the Financial Reporting Oversight Board established by a 2013 Act (profile last updated 16 June 2016)

charts.name: The Gambia reference chart of accounts
charts.legal_reference: There is no legal chart of accounts in The Gambia. The IFRS Foundation's jurisdiction profile says IFRS Standards are required for commercial banks and permitted for all other companies, that SMEs may use the IFRS for SMEs Standard, and that the Companies Act 1955 does not specify the accounting standards to apply; the Gambia Institute of Chartered Accountants (GICA) and the Financial Reporting Oversight Board were created by a 2013 Act, and the profile dates from June 2016, so the current standard-setting position should be confirmed with GICA. This chart is original: four digits, blocked so that each range reaches one line of the IFRS-based statements below, with the accounts a Gambian company actually keeps — VAT input and output tax, import VAT owed to the Gambia Revenue Authority at the border, the net VAT due to or from the Authority after a return, withholding tax, PAYE and social security contributions payable.

numbering.legal_reference: The GRA brochure (§ 7) obliges a VAT registrant to issue VAT-inclusive invoices and receipts, and lists failure to provide VAT invoices, credit notes and debit notes among the offences (§ 15). It prescribes no numbering rule that the pack could read, so `sequential` is the conservative style: a serial number, not a series with no gap.

tax_point.legal_reference: The GRA brochure states no time-of-supply rule, and the Income and Value Added Tax Act, 2012 could not be opened from the machine this pack was written on. `earliest_of_delivery_or_payment` is the pack family's default and is not sourced to the Gambian text; it should be checked against the Act by a local accountant (see the README).

einvoicing.legal_reference: No Gambian text this pack could open obliges a business to exchange a structured electronic invoice: the GRA brochure speaks only of VAT-inclusive invoices and receipts (§ 7), and the Authority's online-services page names no e-invoicing or clearance system. `profile`, `party_scheme` and `vat_scheme` are null and `obligation` is `none`. The absence of a source is not proof that none exists; it is recorded in this pack's README.

not_taxed.legal_reference: Not modelled, for lack of a source — and not a statement that The Gambia leaves the operation untaxed. The GRA brochure (§ 5) says VAT is collected at the point of imports and on domestic taxable supplies, and says nothing about a service bought from a supplier abroad; the Income and Value Added Tax Act, 2012 could not be opened from the machine this pack was written on, and it may well charge the recipient. Until a local accountant confirms the rule against the Act, no purchase tax carries the treatment, and the README lists the gap.
